newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Mr Europe seeks closer UK ties after poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Mr Europe seeks closer UK ties after poll.

text.p: French European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier, praising the Labour party as "quite European", said on Monday he hoped Britain would play a fuller political role in the European Union after a general election due by May.

Barnier, close to Gaullist President Jacques Chirac, accused Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind of electioneering on French soil and said he could not understand why Britain did not take a greater part in political leadership in Europe.

"The British are a great people and a great country, whose economy, we are told, is in good shape. I cannot imagine why they cannot be in the political leadership group of the European Union," he told Reuters in an interview.
"I don't want to interfere in the British election campaign, even if I note that Mr Rifkind came to conduct that campaign outside the United Kingdom from France," Barnier said.

Rifkind, a member of Prime Minister John Major's Conservative party, which is deeply split on Europe, came to Paris last week as part of a European tour to deliver a message criticising the drive for closer EU integration.
Rifkind opposed a "flexibility" clause offered by France and Germany that would allow some countries to move forward on closer integration within the EU without the agreement of all member states.
But Barnier said no single country should be allowed to veto "enhanced cooperation" in areas such as common foreign and security policy.
Asked about Labour's approach, he said he had talked at length with opposition foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook, who was well briefed on the state of EU reform negotiations.

"I note...that Labour is keeping itself very well informed on the negotiations, and we are giving them all the information they want from our side, and that their approach is quite European," the French minister said.
Asked what change he hoped to see from a new British government, Barnier said: "I hope Britain will be a member of the single currency as soon as is politically and technically possible."

Rifkind said recently the British government is "on balance hostile" to joining the planned single currency. Labour has sounded more positive on the issue, while promising a referendum before Britain joined.
French officials now acknowledge it is very unlikely that Britain will join the first wave if Economic and Monetary Union goes ahead on schedule in January 1999.

"I hope that Britain will join the other 14 EU countries in inserting the social chapter into (a reformed EU) treaty. I hope that once the turbulence of the election campaign is over, Britain will take its place and play its role, which should be big, in the political leadership of Europe and not just in its economic management," Barnier said.
Labour is more than 20 percentage points ahead of the Conservatives in opinion polls ahead of the election, which must be held before May 20.

Barnier said he favoured holding a special informal summit in May, once the British election was over, to speed up negotiations on a reform of EU institutions due to be concluded at a regular summit in Amsterdam on June 16-17.
The Dutch EU presidency has said it is considering calling such an informal summit.
